catalog.name: Stock V15
catalog.author: M-VAVE
catalog.tagline: Factory 6-op FM synth: rollback target
catalog.summary: The firmware the FM-1 ships with: Dexed/msfa-derived 6-operator FM, 32 algorithms, 12 voices, arpeggiator, step sequencer and multi-FX. The only firmware the dashboard's Voice and FX editors target. Community firmwares expect you to be on V15 first.
catalog.install: Flash with M-UPGRADE (Windows, in this library after download): extract the zip, run it, load FM-1.fwsc. Most community installers also offer "Return to official V15".

traits.sourceNote: M-VAVE's factory firmware; no source published.
traits.revertNote: This is stock. M-UPGRADE (Windows) reinstalls it, and most community installers can too.
traits.requires_stock_note: This is stock: M-UPGRADE (Windows) installs it over any firmware.

catalog.name: FM-1 Open
catalog.author: M-VAVE
catalog.tagline: Official open firmware + browser workbench
catalog.summary: M-VAVE's official open firmware (October 2026): 6-op FM, 303-style bass, 808-style drums, chiptune, pluck and a sampler on independent tracks. App source is GPLv3 with an SDK linking exception; the sound engine ships as a binary SDK. Free.
catalog.install: Flash and edit from the browser workbench (Chrome/Edge over USB). The release also carries an offline copy of the workbench (HTML) and the development kit.

traits.sourceNote: App source GPLv3 (SDK linking exception); the sound engine is a binary SDK.
traits.revertNote: The workbench's "flash back to stock V15" (刷回原厂 V15) reinstalls V15 and its 128 factory voices.
traits.requires_stock_note: No stock version required: the project's docs don't ask for one before installing.

catalog.name: Felucca
catalog.author: hugelton
catalog.tagline: Multi-engine synth the others build on
catalog.summary: Multi-engine synth by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments): FM, VA, phase distortion, chiptune, sampler, granular, physical modelling, organ and drums; four tracks, 64-step sequencer with conditional steps and Euclid, song mode, MIDI learn, USB audio. The platform most other firmwares are forked from. GPL-3.0.
catalog.install: Web installer (Chrome/Edge, USB) or tools/fm1_install.py. The installer can return to official V15.

traits.revertNote: The installer's "Return to official V15" puts stock back (it asks for your unmodified FM-1.fwsc).
traits.requires_stock_note: No stock version required: the project's docs don't ask for one before installing.

catalog.name: FM-1+VA
catalog.author: Baud Girl
catalog.tagline: The first custom firmware: VA engine + 64-step sequencer
catalog.summary: The first third-party FM-1 firmware, by Madeline (Baud Girl). Keeps the stock FM engine and adds a virtual analog engine (BLEP oscillators, supersaw, several filters), an 8-bit engine with drums and arpeggios, a 64-step dot-matrix sequencer with ratchets and chance, pattern chaining and song mode, four assignable knobs on every screen, two-button navigation and colour themes. Free; closed source (the author has said the source will be released).
catalog.install: Web installer on baudgirl.com (Chrome/Edge on a computer, Chrome on Android). Presets and patterns are kept. No return-to-stock in its installer: use M-UPGRADE with the library's FM-1.fwsc (needs FM-1+VA 94 or later; with 93 or earlier M-UPGRADE fails with "Checksum error"), or another project's "Return to official V15".

traits.sourceNote: Free, closed source; the author has said the source will be released.
traits.revertNote: No return-to-stock in its installer: M-UPGRADE with FM-1.fwsc (FM-1+VA 94 or later), or another installer's "Return to official V15".
traits.requires_stock_note: Installs over stock or other firmware. Its own Version 93 and earlier block M-UPGRADE; update to 94 or later before going back to stock.

catalog.name: April OS
catalog.author: beashoko
catalog.tagline: SK-1-style sampler: record with your phone or laptop mic
catalog.summary: Sampling firmware in the spirit of the Casio SK-1: no synth engines, only samples. 32 sample slots of three seconds, an eight-track sequencer, a sample and loop editor, and recording through a computer's or iPhone's microphone via the installer page. A Felucca fork; its repository holds the installer page, not the firmware source. Free.
catalog.install: Web installer page (Chrome/Edge, USB); the firmware is built into the page, so there is no separate .fwsc to download. No return-to-stock button found: use M-UPGRADE with the library's FM-1.fwsc, or another project's "Return to official V15".

ranking: Live ranking of free, open-source FM-1 firmware, rebuilt on every update check from the cicloid/awesome-fm-1 list (Custom firmware → Open source) and a GitHub repository search, scored ln(1+stars) + ln(1+total .fwsc downloads). Top 10 get cards, #11–#30 the list. Only projects with a GitHub release carrying a .fwsc image count. Free closed-source firmware (FM-1+VA, April OS) has no stars or download counts to compare, so it gets its own curated, unranked section. Paid firmware (Groove OS) is left out. Projects without a curated entry get a card from their GitHub metadata, marked "not curated yet". Offline fallback: firmware/directory.json.

validated.checks: re-test: install, play and revert all clean; boots and plays; presets and the 4 knobs work; MIDI out notes (ch 1-3, 10) and clock seen; generic sound check 1-2 silent by design (ch 1 notes edit the scale); stock sound check 8/8 after revert (run all)
validated.notes: MIDI port 'AMB-1 FM-1' (USB 1209:0001). Re-test: 'Back to the stock firmware' worked first time. In the first session the revert once left a black screen in USB update mode (generic USB-Midi 4D4A:4155); running it again restored stock V15.

validated.checks: boots to ChoralRoot, keys play; generic sound check: heard notes, channel scan, velocity, program change, all notes off; unsure sustain, mod wheel; not heard pitch bend, aftertouch, clock sync, CC probe; sends MIDI clock and notes on ch 1-2; stock sound check 8/8 after revert (run all)
validated.notes: MIDI port 'ChoralRoot FM-1' (USB 1209:0001). It sends its own MIDI clock, so it leads rather than follows external clock. Installed over stock with 'Skip the backup' (stock cannot be backed up); Back up and return to official V15 asks for the unmodified FM-1.fwsc, saves a backup first and worked first time.

validated.checks: installed with ChoralRoot's web installer over stock (Skip the backup), FM-1 answered as FM-1_920; played on the device; generic sound check (run all): heard notes, velocity, sustain, program change, all notes off; unsure channel scan, mod wheel, pitch bend, aftertouch, CC 74 probe; clock sync not heard (ChoralRoot sends its own clock); reverted with Octo-Vave's Install on Stock V15 (FM-1 reports FM-1_015)
validated.notes: MIDI port 'ChoralRoot FM-1'. A chord instrument, not a stock-like synth: several generic MIDI tests have no stock-style mapping, as with 0.25.1. The file matches the release SHA256SUMS and the hash on ChoralRoot's installer page. Installing over stock needs 'Skip the backup' (stock cannot be backed up).

validated.checks: sounds, keys and knobs work; generic sound check 1-4 heard (notes, channels, velocity, sustain); stock steps 1-4 also heard (notes, program change, reverb, distortion); keys sent as MIDI notes on ch 1; stock sound check passed after revert
validated.notes: Under Felucca the FM-1 shows up as MIDI port 'Felucca' (USB 1209:0001, shared with AMB-1) and ignores MIDI identity requests. Return to official V15 asks for the unmodified FM-1.fwsc and saves a full backup first; worked first time. Arpeggiator not figured out during the test.

validated.checks: force flash from stock V15 (FM-1_015) via the V13 workbench; groovebox runs: PLAY, presets, keys, 4 knobs (level, source, step, tempo); generic sound check 1-2 heard; no MIDI out seen; stock sound check passed after revert
validated.notes: Installing from stock needs the workbench's Force flash. Under Open the FM-1 enumerates as USB-Midi (3654:7756) and answers only the workbench's own handshake, not a MIDI identity request. Restore original V15 worked first time and also resets all four voice banks to the 128 factory voices.
